account:
Today has mostly concerned clarifying routine town business rather than any confirmed emergency. I kept tea with the neighbour at the east-dock cottage and returned for the office inspection review, arriving at 16:38. The neighbour said Freight has no confirmed safety complaint, but wants confirmed inspection findings and actual freight orders, especially grain deliveries and contact names. Freight himself advertised an available ferry and freight service. I saw 128 hay bales at the mill stall, but that is stock, not evidence of an order. I have no confirmed grain delivery request.

There has been vague bakery gossip about bridge or port changes, but neither the neighbour nor I has verified any actual change. Builder reported no visible defect at the east ferry landing; this was not a comprehensive structural inspection and does not certify structural soundness. At the inn, the door operated normally and an authorized lantern was supplied and fitted for four emeralds, paid in full. Sleeping arrangements remain unverified, so guest readiness is not certified. Builder intends to make a free initial inquiry for the innkeeper about sourcing one bed; no purchase or paid work has been authorized.

The unusual feature of the afternoon has been confusion over the written record. The secretary initially handed Builder the tea confirmation rather than the inspection report. Builder approved the secretary's oral readback, but explicitly did not verify the written report. I eventually received and read today's report: its main findings match those limitations, but its closing sentence still describes the sixteen-hundred written review as future business. I asked that the actual review time be recorded and requested Builder read the text, but he was no longer visible before I could hand it to him. All four books are now returned to the office chest. I should not describe his oral approval as written verification.

My impression is that the inspections and correspondence are intended to establish what the town can responsibly tell Freight and the innkeeper, and to avoid unnecessary repair spending. There is no confirmed defect, outstanding repair request, or evidence of a concealed project in what I have learned. The main remaining issues are accurate paperwork and the inn's unverified sleeping arrangements.
